summary: A chart stripped to its shape — one series, no axes, no labels, sized to sit beside the number it summarises.

figma.note: Drawn on the Charts page as `Chart / Sparkline`, a Tone variant set. The line, the end dot and the tones are there; pinning the scale across a column is behaviour and is not.

pairs.dont: Let every row scale to its own high and low, so a trunk wobbling by 0.1 draws the same mountain as one that fell by 2.0.
pairs.do: Pass the same `min` and `max` to every sparkline in a column.
pairs.why: A column of sparklines is read by comparing shapes. Auto-scaling each one independently makes every row look equally dramatic, which is the one thing the column was supposed to tell you apart. This is the most common way a sparkline lies.

pairs.dont: Plot a missing reading as 0, so a trunk that stopped reporting draws a cliff to the floor.
pairs.do: Pass `null` and leave the gap. A gap means nobody knows; the floor means someone measured zero.
pairs.why: An endpoint going quiet and an endpoint scoring zero are different incidents with different responses, and a line to the floor reports the second when the first happened.

pairs.dont: Turn the line red and leave it at that.
pairs.do: Keep the badge, the status cell or the icon that says "Critical", and let the tone agree with it.
pairs.why: Status colours are reserved and never travel alone — the same rule KpiTile already follows, for the same reason: colour is not readable by everyone and is gone entirely in a printout.

pairs.dont: Ship the line on its own as the reading.
pairs.do: Put it next to the value it summarises — a KpiTile's number, a table row's figure.
pairs.why: There is no axis, so the line carries direction and steadiness but no magnitude. On its own it says something changed and refuses to say from what to what.

pairs.dont: Add a crosshair, a tooltip or ticks to make it readable point by point.
pairs.do: Use the time-series chart when the values matter, and keep this for the shape.
pairs.why: A crosshair with no axis to read against is furniture pretending to be information, and a 24px-tall plot cannot resolve a value anyway. Growing a sparkline into a chart produces a bad chart rather than a good sparkline.

a11y: `label` is required, and `null` is the explicit way to say the row or tile already names it — there is no default, because a label generated from the numbers would describe the data rather than the point.
With a label it is `role="img"`; with `label={null}` it is `aria-hidden` and nothing is said only by the picture.
The line is 2px at every rendered size (`vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`), so it does not thin out in a narrow column.
A status tone never carries the status alone — see the Do and Don't.
No hover, no focus, nothing interactive: there is nothing to read point by point and nothing to tab to.
